name: Murder of the Universe
artist: King Gizzard and The Lizard Wizard

artist_ref.name: King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard

podcast.body: Released in 2017, this album was considered the least favorite of the band's 2017 output by the speaker due to a narrative voice that was often "heavy" and didn't align well with the music. It also presented three somewhat disconnected stories, making the album feel a bit "strange." "el mar de los de univers pero creo que por culpa de esa voz que están arrando todo el tiempo que a veces es como muy pesada y que no cuadra bien con la música también me dio un poco de pena porque eran como tres historias son tanto inconexas que no terminaba a entender entre ser un disco que se quedaba y un poco raro."

podcast.body: This album, released recently in 2017, is the second installment of a projected five albums the band aimed to release within that year. It has left listeners deeply disconcerted, raising more questions than answers. The album is conceptual, divided into three seemingly independent stories, a format that was popular in the late 1960s but has since declined. Musically, it is described as incredibly complex and well-worked, featuring three distinct styles: epic progressive rock for the first part, epic heavy metal for the central part, and 70s psychedelic rock for the third part, all linked by an interesting musical thread despite the lyrical disconnections. A significant critique is the use of extensive spoken word narration by a man and a woman, which is said to detract from the music. "Este disco así solo te deja con una especie de cara de poquerde no entender nada."
